questions.question: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus, increasing the yield?
questions.solution: (c) Gibberellins. Gibberellins cause internodal elongation, increasing stem length and sugar yield of sugarcane.

questions.topic: Progesterone source and role in pregnancy
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Progesterone is necessary to prevent spontaneous abortion.
Reason (R): Progesterone is secreted by the Graafian follicles.

options.a: A is True, and R is false.
options.b: A is False, and R is true.
options.c: Both A and R are true.
options.d: Both A and R are false.

questions.solution: (a) A is True, and R is false.. Progesterone maintains the uterine lining and pregnancy, so A is true; it is secreted by the corpus luteum (and placenta), not the Graafian follicle (which secretes oestrogen), so R is false.

questions.question: Translocation of carbohydrate nutrients in plants usually occurs in the form of ________.
questions.solution: (d) sucrose. Sugars are transported through the phloem mainly as soluble, non-reducing sucrose.

questions.topic: Number of gamete types from TTRr
questions.question: A plant having the genotype TTRr will produce ________ kinds of gametes.
questions.solution: (d) 2. TT gives only T; Rr gives R or r, so gametes are TR and Tr = 2 kinds (2^n with n = 1 heterozygous pair).

questions.question: A sequence of DNA has 200 nitrogenous bases, of which 60 are Thymine. What is the number of Cytosine in this sequence?

A student half-filled a beaker with solution X. He placed a sealed Visking tubing bag containing solution Y into the beaker. At 30 minutes, the solution in the beaker was orange and the solution inside the Visking tubing was blue-black. What did solutions X and Y contain at the start to give these results?
Options (solution X / solution Y):
A: starch / amylase and iodine
B: iodine / amylase
C: starch and amylase / iodine
D: iodine / starch

options.a: A: X = starch; Y = amylase and iodine
options.c: C: X = starch and amylase; Y = iodine

questions.solution: (d) D: X = iodine; Y = starch. Small iodine molecules diffuse from the beaker into the tubing and turn the starch inside blue-black; large starch molecules cannot pass out, so the beaker stays orange (iodine colour).

questions.question: Urine excretion of sodium ions is regulated by:
questions.solution: (c) Adrenal cortex. The adrenal cortex secretes aldosterone (mineralocorticoid), which regulates Na+ reabsorption/excretion by the kidney.

questions.question: Which would most probably be the genetic makeup of the parents of a colourblind daughter?

options.b: Carrier mother and colour blind father
options.c: Colour blind mother and normal father

questions.solution: (b) Carrier mother and colour blind father. A colour-blind daughter (XcXc) needs an Xc from each parent: father must be colour blind (XcY) and mother at least a carrier (XXc).

questions.question:
Assertion: Compressed natural gas (CNG) is proposed to be a better alternative to fossil fuel.
Reason: Absence of Carbon in CNG.

options.a: Both Assertion and Reason are True.
options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are False.
options.c: Assertion is True and Reason is False.
options.d: Assertion is False and Reason is True.

questions.solution: (c) Assertion is True and Reason is False.. CNG burns more cleanly (less smoke, SO2, unburnt hydrocarbons), so A is true; but CNG is mainly methane (CH4), which contains carbon, so R is false.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true?
(1) The rate of transpiration is influenced by the number of leaves.
(2) The rate of transpiration is influenced by the height of the plant.
(3) The rate of transpiration is influenced by the structure of the leaves.
(4) The rate of transpiration is influenced by the chlorophyll pigment in the cell.
questions.solution: (d) 1,2 and 3.. Leaf number (surface area), plant size/height and leaf structure (cuticle, stomata) affect transpiration; chlorophyll does not.

questions.question: Given below are two stages in the evolution of man (picture A: a stooping man-like figure with heavy brow ridges holding a club; picture B: an ape-like head with protruding jaw). Identify the correct match.
questions.solution: (c) A-Neanderthal, B-Australopithecus. A shows the more human-like Neanderthal man; B shows the ape-like face and projecting jaws of Australopithecus.
questions.figure_desc: Two pictures: A a reconstructed Neanderthal man, B an ape-like Australopithecus head in profile.

questions.question:
Assertion: A convex lens is used to correct hyperopia.
Reason: Image of the object is formed in front of the retina.

options.a: A is True, and R is false.
options.b: A is False, and R is true.
options.c: Both A and R are true.
options.d: Both A and R are false.

questions.solution: (a) A is True, and R is false.. Hyperopia is corrected with a convex lens, so A is true; in hyperopia the image of near objects forms behind the retina (in front of the retina is myopia), so R is false.

questions.question: Why does a reflex arc result in a very quick response? Choose the most appropriate reason.

options.b: because the impulse does not travel to the brain.
options.c: because the motor neurons respond faster than any other.

questions.solution: (b) because the impulse does not travel to the brain.. The response is processed in the spinal cord, so the impulse takes a short path without waiting for the brain.

questions.question:
Tanvi tried to match the phases of menstrual cycle with the number of days as given in the table below:
P - Follicular Phase : Day 5-12
Q - Luteal Phase : Day 15-28
R - Menstrual Phase : Day 3-5
S - Ovulatory Phase : Day 13 or 14
Identify the correct sequence:
questions.solution: (c) R, P, S, Q. The cycle runs menstrual (R) -> follicular/proliferative (P) -> ovulatory (S) -> luteal/secretory (Q).

questions.question: The cell that is impaired, leading to a decrease in blood glucose levels when a patient suffers from a pancreatic disorder.
questions.solution: (b) Alpha. Alpha cells secrete glucagon, which raises blood glucose; if they are impaired, blood glucose falls. (Impaired beta cells would raise blood glucose.)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Abscisic acid is called a growth inhibitor. Justify.
questions.solution: Abscisic acid inhibits/retards growth: it induces dormancy of buds and seeds, inhibits seed germination, causes closure of stomata and promotes ageing and abscission (fall) of leaves and fruits.

marking_points.point: Any one growth-inhibiting effect: induces dormancy of seeds/buds, inhibits germination, closes stomata, or causes leaf/fruit abscission

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Study the reaction that occurs in a plant cell: 2H2O -> 2H+ + O2 + 4e-. Answer the following questions:
a) Explain the given step of photosynthesis.
b) What will be the outcome on the process of photosynthesis, if the hydrogen acceptor is absent in the plant cell? Justify your suggested answer.
questions.solution:
a) This is photolysis of water, a step of the light-dependent (photochemical) phase in the grana: energy absorbed by chlorophyll splits water into H+ ions, electrons and oxygen; O2 is released as a by-product and the electrons replace those lost by chlorophyll.
b) Without the hydrogen acceptor NADP, NADPH2 cannot be formed, so no hydrogen (reducing power) is available for the dark reaction; CO2 cannot be reduced to glucose and photosynthesis (food/sugar formation) stops.

marking_points.point: a) Photolysis of water in light reaction (grana): light energy splits water into H+, e- and O2, O2 released
b) NADP absent -> no NADPH2 -> CO2 not reduced in dark reaction, glucose not formed / photosynthesis stops

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give reasons for the statements:
a) All the food chains begin with green plants.
b) Protein and glucose are not found in urine of a healthy person.
questions.solution:
a) Green plants are the only producers: they trap solar energy and make food by photosynthesis, so all other organisms depend on them directly or indirectly for food/energy.
b) Proteins are large molecules and are not filtered through the glomerulus; glucose is filtered but completely reabsorbed into the blood in the proximal convoluted tubule (selective reabsorption).

marking_points.point: a) Green plants are producers that make food by photosynthesis using sunlight; all consumers depend on them
b) Proteins too large to be filtered; glucose completely reabsorbed in PCT

questions.question:
Which of the following movements are tropic? Identify along with the specific stimulus.
a) Blooming of a flower
b) Twirling of a tendril
c) Pollen tube formation.
questions.solution: Tropic movements: (b) Twirling of a tendril - thigmotropism (stimulus: touch/contact with a support); (c) Growth of pollen tube towards the ovule - chemotropism (stimulus: chemicals/sugars secreted by the ovule). (a) Blooming of a flower is a nastic (non-directional) movement, not tropic.

marking_points.point: Twirling of tendril - thigmotropism (touch/contact)
Pollen tube - chemotropism (chemicals/sugar); blooming is nastic

questions.question: If any leaf of Mimosa (Touch-me-not) is touched, it will fold up within 2-3 seconds. Why?
questions.solution: Touch is a stimulus that causes cells at the base of the leaflets (pulvinus) to lose water and turgor, so the leaflets fold - a seismonastic (thigmonastic) movement due to turgor change.

marking_points.point: Touch causes loss of turgor in pulvinus cells (seismonastic/turgor movement) so leaflets fold

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Discuss how acid rain, a result of air pollution, not only damages ecosystems but also impacts building.
questions.solution: Acid rain forms when SO2 and NOx from burning fuels dissolve in rain to form sulphuric and nitric acids. Ecosystems: it acidifies lakes and soil, killing fish and aquatic life, leaching nutrients and damaging leaves/forests. Buildings: the acids corrode marble and limestone (CaCO3) and metals, e.g. 'marble cancer' of the Taj Mahal, and rust iron structures.

marking_points.point: Effect on ecosystems: acidifies soil/water, kills aquatic life, damages forests/crops
Effect on buildings: corrodes marble/limestone and metals (e.g. Taj Mahal)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Placenta as endocrine gland; transplanting in evening
questions.question:
Give reasons:
a) Placenta acts as an endocrine gland.
b) Farmers usually transplant saplings in a flower bed in the evening.
questions.solution:
a) The placenta secretes hormones such as progesterone, oestrogen and human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) directly into the blood, which maintain pregnancy.
b) In the evening temperature and light are low, so stomata close and transpiration is low; the transplanted sapling, whose roots are damaged and absorb little water, loses less water and does not wilt.

marking_points.point: a) Placenta secretes hormones (progesterone, oestrogen, hCG) into blood
b) Low transpiration in evening reduces water loss/wilting while roots establish

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Explain the terms:
a) Parthenocarpy
b) Root pressure
questions.solution:
a) Parthenocarpy: development of seedless fruits without fertilisation, e.g. induced by auxins/gibberellins (banana, grapes).
b) Root pressure: the pressure developed in the root (xylem) due to continuous entry of water into it by osmosis, which pushes water up the stem.

b) Pressure in root xylem due to continuous inflow of water by osmosis, pushing water upward

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Divya performed an experiment on photosynthesis. At the end of the experiment, she tested the experimental leaf for the presence of starch. During the starch test she first boiled the leaf in water and then in methylated spirit.
(a) Why did she boil the leaf in water?
(b) Mention the reason why she then boiled the leaf in methylated spirit.
questions.solution:
(a) Boiling in water kills the cells, stops all chemical (enzymatic) reactions and softens the leaf/breaks cell membranes so iodine can penetrate.
(b) Methylated spirit dissolves the chlorophyll and decolourises the leaf, so the blue-black colour of the iodine test is clearly seen.

marking_points.point: (a) Kills cells/stops reactions and softens leaf
(b) Removes chlorophyll (decolourises) so colour change is visible

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question:
The diagram represents a stage during cell division (chromosomes pulled to the two poles by spindle fibres, with a constriction appearing in the cell). Study the same and then answer the questions that follow:
a) Identify the given stage of mitosis and support your answer with a reason.
b) Name the stage that comes after the above stage and draw a labelled diagram to represent the same.
questions.solution:
a) Anaphase (late): the centromeres have split and the daughter chromosomes are pulled by the shortening spindle fibres to opposite poles; a furrow is beginning.
b) Telophase. Diagram: two groups of chromosomes at opposite poles, uncoiling; nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappearing around each group; spindle disappearing; cleavage furrow deepening. Labels: nuclear membrane, nucleolus, chromosomes/chromatin, cleavage furrow, centriole.

marking_points.point: a) Anaphase with reason: chromatids/daughter chromosomes moving to opposite poles
b) Telophase named with a correctly labelled diagram (nuclear membrane reforming, furrow)

questions.figure_desc: Animal cell in late anaphase: two groups of chromosomes pulled to opposite poles by spindle fibres, asters at poles, slight furrow.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Demography vs natality; potometer vs osmoscope
questions.question:
Distinguish between the following:
a) Demography and Natality [Definition]
b) Potometer and an osmoscope [function]
questions.solution:
a) Demography: the statistical study of human populations (size, density, distribution, births, deaths). Natality: the birth rate, i.e. number of live births per 1000 people per year.
b) Potometer: measures the rate of water uptake (transpiration) by a plant shoot. Osmoscope (thistle funnel set-up): demonstrates osmosis.

marking_points.point: a) Demography = statistical study of population; natality = births per 1000 per year
b) Potometer measures rate of transpiration/water uptake; osmoscope demonstrates osmosis

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Observe the diagram given below (section of testis within the scrotum, parts labelled 1-4) and answer the questions that follow.
a) Label the parts 1 and 2.
b) State effect of non-functioning part 4 on - 1) sperm production 2) semen formation.
c) Explain - vasectomy.
questions.solution:
a) 1 - Scrotum (scrotal sac); 2 - Seminiferous tubules (testis lobules).
b) Part 4 is the epididymis. 1) Sperm production in the seminiferous tubules continues, but sperms are not stored or matured (they do not become motile). 2) Semen is still formed from secretions of seminal vesicles, prostate and Cowper's glands, but it lacks mature/functional sperms, so the person is infertile.
c) Vasectomy: a surgical method of male sterilisation in which a small part of each vas deferens (3) is cut and tied, so sperms cannot reach the urethra/semen.

marking_points.point: a) 1 scrotum, 2 seminiferous tubules
b) Sperm still produced but not matured/stored; semen formed without functional sperms
c) Vas deferens cut and tied - male sterilisation

questions.figure_desc: Section of testis in scrotum: 1 scrotal wall, 2 seminiferous tubules/lobules, 3 vas deferens, 4 epididymis.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A special indicator paper is blue when dry but turns pink when wet. In an experiment, some dry papers were attached to the upper and lower surfaces of a leaf on plants A and B. The graph given below shows the results for the upper and lower surface of each plant, A and B. The y axis shows the time taken for the paper to turn pink.
Graph (time taken to turn pink): Plant A - upper surface about 3, lower surface about 3; Plant B - upper surface about 10, lower surface about 6.
a) Name the indicator paper used in the given experiment.
b) Suggest a reason to explain this difference in water loss between the upper and lower leaf surfaces of plant A and B.
questions.solution:
a) Cobalt chloride paper.
b) Plant A: both surfaces turned pink in the same short time, so stomata are equally distributed on both surfaces (isobilateral leaf, e.g. monocot like grass/maize). Plant B: lower surface turned pink much faster than upper, so it has more stomata on the lower surface and fewer on the upper surface, which also has a thicker cuticle (dorsiventral dicot leaf); hence more water is lost from the lower surface.

marking_points.point: a) Cobalt chloride paper
b) Plant A: stomata equally distributed on both surfaces (isobilateral)
Plant B: more stomata on lower surface / thicker cuticle on upper (dorsiventral)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: The S phase of a cell cycle occurs during interphase, before mitosis. Give reason.
questions.solution: In the S (synthesis) phase DNA replicates so that each chromosome has two identical chromatids; this must happen before mitosis so that each daughter cell receives a complete, identical set of chromosomes.

marking_points.point: DNA replicates in S phase so each daughter cell gets identical full set of chromosomes

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: How does the ozone layer depletion affect life on earth?
questions.solution: The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays. Its depletion (by CFCs etc.) allows more UV radiation to reach the earth, causing skin cancer, cataract and weakened immunity in humans, damage to crops/plankton and reduced productivity, and mutations in living organisms.

marking_points.point: Depletion lets more harmful UV rays reach the earth
Effects: skin cancer, cataract, lowered immunity, damage to plants/plankton (any one or two)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: If you could override the control mechanisms that open stomata and force them to remain closed what would you expect to happen to the plant? Discuss 2 probable outcomes with valid reason.
questions.solution: 1. Photosynthesis would stop/decrease because CO2 cannot enter the leaf; the plant would starve. 2. Transpiration would stop, so the transpiration pull and ascent of sap/mineral transport would decrease and the leaves would overheat (no cooling effect). (Also gaseous exchange for respiration would be hampered.)

marking_points.point: Photosynthesis stops as CO2 cannot enter
Transpiration stops: no cooling/no transpiration pull, so less water and mineral uptake

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: Give the composition of - a) nucleosome b) nucleotide
questions.solution:
a) Nucleosome: a core of eight histone protein molecules (octamer) around which DNA is wrapped (about two turns), linked by linker DNA.
b) Nucleotide: a pentose (deoxyribose) sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base (A, T, G or C).

marking_points.point: a) DNA coiled around a core of 8 histone proteins
b) Deoxyribose sugar + phosphate + nitrogenous base

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Two potato cubes each 1 cm3 in size, were placed separately in two containers (A and B), the container (A) having solution I and the other (B) containing solution II. After 24 hours when the cubes were examined, those placed in container A were found to be firm and had increased slightly in size and those placed in container B were found to be soft and had decreased in size. Use the above information to answer the questions that follow:
(i) Account for the firmness and increase in size of the potato cubes which were placed in solution I.
(ii) Account for the softness and decrease in size of the potato cubes which were placed in solution II.
(iii) Discuss the probable observation with reason for the given condition - boiled potato cubes are placed in solution I.
questions.solution:
(i) Solution I is hypotonic (e.g. water/dilute solution): water enters the potato cells by endosmosis, cells become turgid, so cubes are firm and larger.
(ii) Solution II is hypertonic (concentrated salt/sugar solution): water leaves the cells by exosmosis, cells become flaccid/plasmolysed, so cubes are soft and smaller.
(iii) No change in firmness or size: boiling kills the cells and destroys the selectively permeable cell membrane, so osmosis does not occur.

marking_points.point: (i) Hypotonic solution; endosmosis makes cells turgid
(ii) Hypertonic solution; exosmosis makes cells flaccid/plasmolysed
(iii) No change as boiled cells' membranes are dead/not selectively permeable, so no osmosis
